title: Embeddings / Rerank: protocol harmonization for pagination and HTTP error mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Align Redwood's new unified embeddings/rerank endpoints with legacy client expectations for pagination cursors and HTTP error semantics, while preserving improvements (stable cursors, idempotency, clearer retry guidance) so existing customers experience minimal disruption. This ticket covers the protocol mapping spec, migration playbook for legacy clients, test harnesses, backwards-compatible server behavior, and rollout gating.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts legacy cursor token formats (base64 v1 and v2) for a transition period and returns normalized cursor fields in responses.
HTTP error mapping table implemented: legacy 400/401/429/5xx codes map to documented new API errors and include stable machine-readable 'code' and human 'message'.
SDKs (python, js) include adapters that translate legacy client retry logic to Redwood recommended patterns and expose deprecation warnings at runtime.
End-to-end compatibility tests exist for: cursor round-trip, page size boundaries, cursor expiry, transparent fallback to stateless pagination, and rate-limit window semantics.
Migration playbook published with step-by-step verification, sample curl commands, and a canary checklist for customers moving to the unified endpoint.
decisions: Use a versioned cursor envelope: {"v": "2", "payload": "<opaque>"} encoded server-side; still accept legacy v1 tokens for 6 months.
Normalise error surface: always return JSON {"code": <string>, "message": <string>, "retry_after": <int seconds optional>} for all non-2xx responses.
Maintain stable sort by document score for rerank across pages; include last_score in cursor to detect drift and surface warning to clients if unstable.
Expose a migration feature flag (internal) to toggle strict-mode which rejects legacy cursors during canary rollout.
tasks: Draft protocol mapping doc and publish to Confluence (owner: PM).
ENG: implement dual-acceptor cursor parser on server + normalized cursor response header (X-Redwood-Cursor).
SDK: add legacy adapter in python/js that warns when legacy cursor used and auto-converts v1->v2.
E2E: add tests in integration suite for cursor expiry, page boundaries, and 429 handling across different client request patterns.
Docs: update API reference with explicit HTTP mapping table and migration steps.
Solutions: prepare customer-facing migration guide and sample commands for top-10 customers impacted.
notes: Trade-offs considered: keeping legacy cursor format forever reduces operational complexity for customers but hampers ability to iterate on cursor semantics (e.g., adding last_score). We chose a timeboxed dual-accept strategy to balance iteration speed and customer stability. We also debated exposing 'retry_after' only on 429 vs. including it on 503; consensus: include when known but never on 4xx non-rate-limit errors.
